about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Corn gapped higher and held most of it into the short-session close, with Dec settling near 446.75 just above new 445 support; the move tracked the soy complex and pre-holiday export interest rather than any change to the large US crop.
events: Corn and soybeans gap higher in Friday's short session (Successful Farming)
Dec ~446.75, testing 449.5 resistance (CBOT)
Traders ask whether corn and soy broke out to end the week (Barchart)

soybeans.fundamental: Jan beans pushed through 1,269.5 early but faded into the close at about 1,266, back under that resistance; crush demand for biofuel oil and the firmer real remain the support, while Mato Grosso rains limit the Brazil weather premium.
events: Jan settles ~1,266 after early high above 1,269.5 (CBOT)
Rains ease El Niño fears in Mato Grosso (Bloomberg)
Biofuels boom supports soybeans (Brownfield)

meal.fundamental: Spread trade points to strong end-user meal demand, which is absorbing the heavy crush output better than expected; Dec meal at about 366 sits just under 369 resistance.
events: Grain spreads flag impressive meal demand (Barchart)
Dec ~366.3, below 369.1 resistance (CBOT)
Soy complex gaps higher Friday (Successful Farming)

oil.fundamental: Biofuel demand is the support story for soyoil, while stalled Indonesian palm tenders on weak demand show the veg-oil complex is not tight; crude's intraday drop is a headwind for biodiesel margins.
events: Biofuels boom supports soy complex (Brownfield)
Indonesia palm oil tenders stall on weak demand (Bloomberg)
WTI ~82.8 (-1.9%) (OilPrice)

palm.fundamental: Stalled Indonesian tenders point to soft export demand even with tight local supply, and crude's intraday reversal removes part of the biodiesel support; India's shift back toward palm remains the main offset.

natgas.fundamental: No US supply shock; abroad, Australia's 20% domestic reservation law and Russia-China pricing friction are longer-term LNG-market stories rather than near-term US demand drivers.

crude.fundamental: WTI recovered from the midday dip to about 83 at the close, back above 82.83 support; Iraq is pushing OPEC for a higher quota as it lifts exports, which adds to doubts over quota discipline ahead of the 2027 capacity review, while stockpiling demand is cited as a floor.
events: Iraq presses OPEC for a higher production ceiling (Bloomberg, OilPrice)
WTI Jan ~83.1, back above 82.83 support (NYMEX)
US urged Iraq and Venezuela to weigh leaving OPEC (Reuters)

ulsd.fundamental: Distillates stay the firm part of the barrel: Russia extended its jet-fuel export ban to March after refinery attacks, and the global diesel balance is seen moving into deficit by Q2 2027. Refinery outages at Jazan and Amuay add to that.
events: Russia extends jet fuel export ban to March (Bloomberg)
Global diesel market seen in deficit in Q2 2027 (Reuters)
Attack halts part of Aramco's Jazan refinery (Reuters)

rbob.fundamental: Gasoline remains the weak link of the barrel in the seasonal demand trough; crude-led strength is lifting it in sympathy rather than any change in gasoline balances.
events: Gasoline falling while diesel stays expensive (OilPrice)
